title: Qualify exact pointwise real derivative, nondifferentiability and domain refusals
commitMessage: feat: qualify exact pointwise derivative domains and close M4 W02 C01

contribution.summary: Qualify M4-W02-C01-T2 through a compiled absent-API RED, 37 independent GREEN tests and eight NuGet-only consumer probes. Deliver exact-rational pointwise derivative evaluation over T1's proven polynomial rules, with typed nondifferentiability at the real absolute/sqrt-square kink, original rational pole exclusions, sqrt real-domain boundaries, unit and assumption refusals. Inspect three local NuGet packages and close only C01 while keeping W02/M4 active.
contribution.value: Make an exact real point derivative distinguishable from a nondifferentiable point, undefined original domain and unknown analytic operation, without finite differences, dropped restrictions or general CAS claims.
debtChanges: One real compiled missing-API RED precedes installation of the exact pointwise product and preview.6 project version.

37 GREEN tests cover exact polynomial derivative values, absent target, rational point, local real absolute/sqrt-square rules, kink and root-domain refusals, original quotient holes, units and assumptions.
An admitted pointwise value carries its rule ID, original math-ir/1 structural source hash and differentiation target identity; every refusal has no value or proof.
Conservative 128-bit rational and existing IR graph limits prevent unbounded exact evaluation; unsupported radical and quotient derivative forms never fall back to binary64.
Eight independent local NuGet-only probes validate exact cubic slope, absent symbol, kink, domain and dimensional refusals through one pinned symbolics preview.6 package.
Three local Math product archives have separate C# manifest, dependency, net10 assembly, byte-length and SHA-256 checks; no DWF authority is rehashed or package publicly released.
Finish only C01-T2 R/G/V, T2 and C01 after relevant symbolics/IR/quantities regressions; W02 stays in-progress, C02/C03 not-ready, with no AURA/dw.discovery/Decision integration.
